title: Approve an invoice: pick the APPROVED rubber stamp by its label, ink it, hold the sheet, stamp squarely in the box
context: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics counts 1,532,400 bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerks (Occupational Outlook Handbook, 2025). Their listed duties include receiving and recording vouchers and checking documents for accuracy; on paper, a checked invoice is marked with a rubber stamp (approved, paid, received), as it also is in mail rooms, warehouses and clinics. The job has what a desk robot finds hard: the stamps look alike and differ only by a printed word, a stamp works only after a second step (the ink pad), the print must land flat, square and inside a 5 cm box, the loose invoice book slides unless the other hand holds it, and a wrong stamp on a document cannot be undone. Here an A5 invoice book lies loose on a desk pad, the approval box of its top invoice empty. A rack holds three wooden rubber stamps labelled REJECTED (red), APPROVED (green) and COPY (blue); an open ink pad lies beside it. The instruction names neither the stamp nor the box.
setup: Counter top is z = 0.7475 m; positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left. All real size; shapes are CAD models. (1) Desk pad, fixed: dark green leatherette, 300 (x) x 460 (y) x 2 mm, centre (0.37, 0.10). (2) Invoice book, free: an A5 pad of invoices glued at its top edge, 148 x 210 x 4 mm, about 90 g, lying loose on the desk pad, centre (0.345, 0.07), long side along x; its top invoice (called the sheet below) has its text reading toward -y (left to right as seen from the robot), top of the page at the far edge; printed header, four item lines with amounts, a total, and at its near right corner an empty box 50 x 50 mm headed APPROVAL, centre (0.280, 0.033). (3) Stamp rack, fixed: walnut tray 150 (x) x 76 (y) x 12 mm at (0.40, -0.185) with three felt-lined pockets 32 x 56 mm. (4) Three wooden rubber stamps, free, standing in the pockets at x = 0.354, 0.400, 0.446, y = -0.185: each 75 mm tall, about 60 g, rubber face 20 (x) x 44 (y) mm, wooden mount 26 x 50 mm, handle 24 x 46 mm with a flat top carrying a coloured label 20 x 42 mm with white capitals 7.5 mm tall, facing straight up and reading from the robot's left to its right: nearest REJECTED (red), middle APPROVED (green), farthest COPY (blue). The words are legible in the overview picture and from a wrist camera within about 15 cm; in the 640-pixel top camera the labels are told apart by colour and position, the words are too small to read there. Apart from the label they are identical. The printed word runs along the long side of the face, the same way round as the label. (5) Ink pad, fixed: blue tin 70 (x) x 110 (y) mm at (0.275, -0.310), lying open, its dark felt 64 x 104 mm standing 13 mm above the counter; its lid lies open behind it. (6) A ballpoint pen on the desk pad at (0.47, 0.255), dressing. Real trial props (all low cost): STAMPS: three made-to-order wooden-mount rubber stamps (any stamp shop) with a 20 x 44 mm rubber die on 2.5 mm foam, the words APPROVED, REJECTED and COPY each inside a 16 x 40 mm frame; mount and handle of planed beech, 50 x 26 mm foot, 24 x 46 mm handle, 75 mm tall overall, 60 g (+/- 10 g, kitchen scale); a paper label 20 x 42 mm glued on the handle top, white capitals 7.5 mm tall on green, red and blue, reading the same way round as the die. INK PAD: an ordinary felt office stamp pad in a hinged tin about 70 x 110 mm, black water-based ink, taped to the counter. INVOICE BOOK: the invoice layout printed 25 times on 80 g A5 paper, glued along the top edge to a 0.6 mm greyboard back (padding glue), 4 mm thick, about 90 g; on the desk pad it should start to slide at 0.3 to 0.5 N of sideways pull (spring scale). RACK: a 150 x 76 x 12 mm wooden block with three 32 x 56 mm pockets 6 mm deep, taped down. Positions are fixed with 3 mm masking tape: the desk pad's corners on the counter, and four L-shaped corner marks for the book on the desk pad, each with a second tick 10 mm outside it.
scoring: Read every step from measured poses and from the disclosed ink rule. Rule: a stamp is inked once its rubber face has been pressed on the ink pad (whole face inside the felt's outline and within 2 mm of it, stamp upright within 15 degrees), and it stays inked. Each time an inked stamp's face touches the top invoice (any corner or the centre of the face over the page and within 1.5 mm of it, at any tilt) it leaves one mark, until it is lifted 3 mm clear: one press, one mark, however long it is held; a second press is a second mark, re-inked or not. A mark's place and angle are the stamp's when most of its face was down; it is whole if all four corners of the face were down at once, and smeared if the stamp slid more than 4 mm over the page while touching. A dry stamp leaves nothing. Marks are measured in the book's own frame, so they move with it. Any REJECTED or COPY mark on the invoice, whole or partial, at any time, scores 0 for the trial (latched); inking those stamps or printing them on the desk pad does not. Otherwise 0.5: an APPROVED mark whose centre is inside the approval box. 1.0: exactly one mark on the invoice, the APPROVED one, whole and not smeared, all four corners of its 40 x 16 mm outline inside the box, its text within 20 degrees of the page's text (not upside down), the invoice book left where it lay on the desk pad (all of it on the pad, moved less than 10 mm and turned less than 5 degrees), the other two stamps still standing in the rack, and the APPROVED stamp put down, not dropped, off the book (in the rack or on the desk, at rest, both grasp points at least 7 cm from its handle), all held 1 s. Two marks score at most 0.5. Doing nothing scores 0. Holding the book is not scored by itself: it is what keeps the box where the stamp is aimed and the book in its place when the stamp lands or lifts off askew. Reported: inked, marks, mark_whole, mark_smear_mm, mark_offset_mm, mark_angle_deg, prints_off_sheet (inked stamps touched to the desk pad or counter), sheet_shift_mm, sheet_turn_deg, stamp_in_rack, dropped. Real trial: the same rule, read from the video and from a photo taken straight down on the book afterwards with a ruler lying beside the box (the printed box, 50 mm, is the scale). A mark is any visible ink print a stamp left on the top invoice, faint or partial included; which stamp made it is read from the video (label colour) and from the printed word. The zero is the moment a REJECTED or COPY print appears on the invoice; the starting state (clean invoice, dry stamps) is not a zero condition. 0.5: an APPROVED print whose frame centre is inside the box lines. 1.0: exactly one print on the invoice, the APPROVED one, its whole frame and word printed and not dragged (no ghost edge wider than 4 mm), all four corners of its 40 x 16 mm frame inside the box lines, the frame's long side within 20 degrees of the box's lower line (protractor on the photo) and the word upright, every corner of the book still inside its 10 mm tick marks and its edge within 5 degrees of the tape, the other two stamps still standing in the rack, and the stamp put down by the hand (not dropped), standing or lying off the book with both grippers at least 7 cm from its handle for 1 s. A second visible print, however faint, is a second mark. A press with a dry stamp leaves nothing and costs nothing. Ink prints on the desk pad are noted, not scored.
reset_notes: Fixed starting poses, no randomisation; arms at the ready pose; all three stamps dry. Real trial reset: tear off the stamped invoice so the book shows a clean one (replace the book when it is under 3 mm thick); push the book into its four tape corners; blot every stamp on scrap paper until it leaves no print (a stamp is inked only by being pressed on the pad during the trial); stand the stamps in their pockets in the order REJECTED, APPROVED, COPY, labels reading toward the robot's right; open the ink pad. Ink pad: keep the tin closed between sessions, at room temperature; before each session make one test print on scrap paper with a spare stamp pressed at about 10 N (kitchen scale under the pad): it must be fully legible, otherwise re-ink the felt; re-ink after about 200 prints or one month; do not leave the tin open for more than 2 hours.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, rigid bodies. The invoice book is one rigid block (4 mm, 90 g): it slides and turns; its pages cannot bend or lift. Ink is a rule on measured poses, not a fluid: it never runs out or transfers between objects; a mark is always drawn as the stamp's whole framed word in its label colour (a real pad gives one colour). Stamps, rack, ink pad and desk pad are boxes under the CAD visuals (rack pockets 1 mm wider all round than drawn). Labels and print are thin coloured geometry.
